## Highlights

- Every `fin_*` function now computes the model its name promises. Technical indicators follow TA-Lib, statistical tests return p-values, portfolio optimizers solve their objectives, and curve bootstrapping prices deposits, FRAs and swaps. The experimental catalog is empty. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90), [#91](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/91), [#92](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/92), [#93](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/93), [#94](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/94), [#95](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/95), [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
- Results no longer depend on thread count or physical row order. Order-dependent functions take an explicit ordering column or `ORDER BY` inside the call, and rolling indicators work both grouped and with `OVER (... ORDER BY ...)`.
- Built for DuckDB v1.5.6, with faster scalars and lower memory use for volume profiles, grids and windowed aggregates. [#89](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/89)

## Upgrading from 0.2.x

0.3.0 is a breaking release. Many functions now require an ordering argument, several signatures changed, and functions that used to return placeholder values now return real results. Queries that ran on 0.2.x can fail to bind or return different numbers.

1. Use DuckDB v1.5.6. Release artifacts are built for that version only.
2. Update the extension: `FORCE INSTALL finance FROM community;` (or `UPDATE EXTENSIONS (finance);`), then `LOAD finance;`.
3. Search your SQL for the functions listed under [Compatibility](#compatibility) and update the calls. The most common change is adding a timestamp argument (`fin_delta(x, ts)`) or `ORDER BY ts` inside an aggregate (`fin_atr(high, low, close, 14 ORDER BY ts)`).
4. Replace `name := value` arguments on native functions with positional arguments. Macros still accept named parameters.
5. Re-run reports and compare against 0.2.x output before relying on them. Changed numbers are expected wherever a function previously returned a placeholder or a simplified formula.

Changes to check first:
- [Ordering is now explicit](#ordering-is-now-explicit)
- [Changed signatures](#changed-signatures)
- [Errors and NULL handling](#errors-and-null-handling)

## Features

- Technical indicators are native aggregates that match TA-Lib 0.6 on grouped and running-window values, including warm-up periods. [#93](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/93), [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
  - Trend and momentum: SMA, EMA, WMA, DEMA, TEMA, TRIMA, T3, KAMA, HMA, MACD, APO, PPO, RSI, stochastic, stochastic RSI, Aroon, CCI, Bollinger and Keltner bands, SAR, linear regression, TRIX and the ROC family.
  - Volume and direction: true range, ATR, NATR, ±DM, ±DI, DX, ADX, ADXR, MFI, ultimate oscillator, OBV, AD line and ADOSC.
- Microstructure functions follow their published definitions: Lee-Ready trade signing (with the previous touch rule as `'emo'`), Roll spread, VPIN with volume buckets, time-weighted TWAP and a bounded-memory volume profile. [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
- Statistical tests return a statistic and a p-value: t-tests, Welch, z-test, ANOVA, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Mann-Whitney U, Ljung-Box and ADF. Newey-West HAC t-statistics, Cramér's V, Theil's U, mutual information, OLS, Hurst, half-life, autocorrelation and rank correlation are implemented. [#94](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/94)
- Portfolio construction solves its objectives: minimum variance, maximum Sharpe, risk parity, Black-Litterman, hierarchical risk parity, efficient frontier, `fin_portfolio_optimize`, Fama-MacBeth and GARCH(1,1) fitting. Covariance and correlation matrices return `STRUCT(labels, matrix)`. [#92](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/92), [#94](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/94)
- `fin_bootstrap_curve` bootstraps discount factors from deposit, FRA, par swap and zero quotes with log-linear discount interpolation, matching QuantLib. [#95](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/95)
- Business-day and session functions apply the NYSE holiday calendar, early closes and time zones. [#91](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/91)
- Bars follow the AFML reset rules and return `bar_id` and `ticks`. Imbalance bars take an explicit threshold. [#92](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/92)
- Exponential-decay aggregates (`fin_ema_halflife`, `fin_exp_decay_*`) apply half-life weights to timestamps or numeric axes. [#94](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/94)

## Bug Fixes

- Returns and risk aggregates no longer change with thread count. Sortino, Omega, alpha and downside measures convert annual thresholds geometrically. Gain to pain, log NAV, drawdown at risk, Yang-Zhang volatility and the GARCH forecast now compute their documented formulas. Parametric VaR and CVaR honor the distribution argument. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90)
- Options and rates return correct values. [#91](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/91)
  - Rho in market units is scaled by 1/100 (was 1/10000).
  - `fin_bsm_color` has the correct sign.
  - `fin_bsm_prob_touch` is exact.
  - `fin_accrued_interest` matches QuantLib.
  - `30U/360` uses the SIA rules instead of Bond Basis.
  - Digital and probability-ITM functions return values at expiry instead of NULL.
- `fin_rate` applies its unit argument. `fin_changes` and `fin_resets` count consecutive changes and decreases. [#92](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/92)
- Grids skip NULL values, anchor month steps at the start timestamp and reject invalid configurations. Schema validation checks real column types. [#92](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/92)
- `fin_data_quality_report` computes `min` and `max` over finite values. A NaN input used to make `max` NaN. [#RELEASE_PR](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/RELEASE_PR)
- Bid/ask helpers return NULL for crossed quotes, negative sizes and empty books instead of misleading numbers. [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)

## Compatibility

### Ordering is now explicit

- Add a timestamp argument to these macros. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90), [#92](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/92), [#94](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/94), [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
  - `fin_calmar(r, ts, ann)`, `fin_recovery_factor(r, ts)`, `fin_zscore_last(x, ts)`, `fin_rolling_zscore(x, ts)`
  - `fin_delta`, `fin_pct_change`, `fin_changes`, `fin_resets`, `fin_first_non_null`, `fin_last_non_null`: `(x)` becomes `(x, ts)`
  - `fin_autocorr`, `fin_crosscorr`, `fin_hurst`, `fin_half_life_mean_reversion`, `fin_adf`, `fin_ljung_box`, `fin_newey_west_tstat`
  - `fin_ohlc(price, ts)` and `fin_ohlcv(price, volume, ts)`
- Add `ORDER BY ts` inside the call, or use a window ordered by time, for every technical indicator and for `fin_drawdown_at_risk`, `fin_conditional_drawdown_at_risk`, `fin_garch11_forecast`, `fin_yang_zhang_vol`, `fin_stability`, `fin_vpin` and `fin_twap`. A grouped call without `ORDER BY` raises "rows reached the aggregate in an undefined order" when DuckDB merges partial results in parallel. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90), [#93](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/93), [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
- Indicators return NULL until their TA-Lib lookback is filled. `fin_ema` is seeded with the SMA of the first `period` values instead of the first observation. [#93](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/93)
- Ties on the ordering key resolve deterministically: the first value takes the smaller and the last value takes the larger of tied rows. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90)

### Changed signatures

- `fin_aggregate_return(r, period_key, method)` becomes `fin_aggregate_return(r, method)`. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90)
- `fin_kyle_lambda(signed_volume, price_change)` becomes `fin_kyle_lambda(price_change, signed_volume)`, matching `fin_beta`. [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
- `fin_vpin(signed_volume, volume, buckets)` becomes `fin_vpin(signed_volume, volume, buckets, bucket_volume ORDER BY ts)`. [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
- `fin_ppo` and `fin_apo` take `ma_type` (`'sma'` or `'ema'`) instead of a signal period. `fin_sarext` takes the TA-Lib parameter list instead of an options value. `fin_bbands` gains a `ddof` argument, and `fin_bbands`, `fin_stddev` and `fin_var_indicator` default to population deviation. [#93](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/93)
- `fin_stoch` returns the slow stochastic and `fin_stochrsi` returns `STRUCT(k, d)`. [#93](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/93)
- `fin_volume_profile` returns `LIST(STRUCT(price_low, price_high, volume))` instead of a price histogram `MAP`. `fin_bop` is a per-bar scalar. [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
- `fin_cov_matrix` and `fin_corr_matrix` take `(ts, asset, r)`. `fin_factor_turnover` takes `(ts, asset, factor, period)`. `fin_black_litterman_returns` adds `risk_aversion`. `fin_linear_trend` requires `x`. `fin_ztest_mean` returns a STRUCT, and t-test `df` is DOUBLE. [#94](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/94)
- `fin_garch_fit` requires `order_col` as its third argument. `fin_fama_macbeth` returns one row per coefficient. `fin_portfolio_optimize` and `fin_portfolio_optimize_table` return solved weights. [#94](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/94)
- `fin_bootstrap_curve` and `fin_curve_bootstrap` take the instrument type (`deposit`, `fra`, `swap`, `zero`) as the second argument. Pass instrument names with `instrument_col :=`. Output adds `instrument_type`, `rate` and `forward_rate`. [#95](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/95)
- `fin_imbalance_bars` requires a `threshold`. `fin_predict_linear_to_grid` requires a `lookback` interval. Bar, grid, normalizer, `fin_validate_schema`, `fin_factor_report`, `fin_hrp_weights` and `fin_efficient_frontier` outputs gain or rename columns. [#92](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/92)
- `fin_npv(cfs, times, rate)` defaults to periodic compounding (was continuous). `fin_nearest_psd` defaults to eigenvalue clipping. `fin_trade_sign` defaults to Lee-Ready. [#91](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/91), [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
- Integer parameters are BIGINT. The `fin_equal_weights` INTEGER overload is removed. Native functions reject `name := value` arguments. The internal helpers `finance_{cvar,trimmed_mean,winsorized_mean,weighted_quantile}_internal` are removed. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90), [#91](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/91)

### Errors and NULL handling

- Invalid constant configuration raises an error that starts with the function name, for example an unknown method, day count, compounding, calendar or unit, a VaR confidence outside (0, 1), or an out-of-range period. Before, several of these returned NULL or silently used a default. `'bermudan'` exercise is rejected. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90), [#91](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/91), [#93](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/93)
- Per-row domain problems return NULL instead of raising: invalid OHLC bars, expired options, missing IRR roots, crossed quotes and non-finite inputs. Groups containing NaN or infinity return NULL. [#90](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/90), [#91](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/91), [#96](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/96)
- Rate-of-change indicators, PPO and TRIX return NULL on a zero base (TA-Lib returns 0). [#93](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/93)
- Table functions raise errors on duplicate keys, such as duplicate curve maturities or duplicate portfolio rows. [#92](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/92), [#95](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/95)

## Tooling and Release

- Build and release against DuckDB v1.5.6 with extension-ci-tools v1.5.6. [#89](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/89)
- `duckdb_functions()` shows a specific description, the real parameter names of each overload and a self-contained example for every `fin_*` function. CI runs all 383 examples. [#88](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/88), [#RELEASE_PR](https://github.com/leonardovida/duckdb-finance/pull/RELEASE_PR)
- Align source, community-manifest and package metadata at 0.3.0.

## Validation

- Technical indicators match TA-Lib on every row of grouped and running-window references. Curve bootstrapping matches QuantLib 1.43 within 1e-14. Statistical tests, regressions and optimizers were checked against scipy and numpy.
- Debug smoke, gold and numerical checks pass locally on DuckDB v1.5.6, including 618 numerical reference comparisons, and under an UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer build. Linux CI builds with GCC and UBSan.
- Order-dependent functions give identical results with 1 and 8 threads.
